# Mathematical notation and reasoning {#sec-math-system}

This chapter defines the shared authoring contract for mathematical prose,
display equations, structured notation, and formal reasoning. Authors write
portable TeX mathematics in Markdown; backend-specific commands are not part
of the manuscript contract.

## Inline and display mathematics {#sec-math-inline-display}

Inline expressions such as [$E_k = \tfrac{1}{2} m v^2$]{.alkahest-math-alt alt="kinetic energy at step k equals one half mass times velocity squared"} belong grammatically to
their sentence and should align with the surrounding text. Use a display when
an expression needs a stable reference, a multi-line derivation, or enough
space to expose its structure.

Every important display receives an `eq-` identifier and a concise plain-text
description. The description states the equation's purpose instead of trying
to pronounce every symbol.

## Aligned equations {#sec-math-aligned}

One aligned block receives one equation number. Alignment points communicate
the relationship between lines without inserting spaces by hand:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{x}_{k+1} &= A\mathbf{x}_k + B\mathbf{u}_k, \\
\mathbf{y}_k     &= C\mathbf{x}_k + D\mathbf{u}_k.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-state-update alt="Discrete state-space update and output equations"}

@eq-state-update is the canonical aligned-equation fixture. Independent
relationships that need separate references should be separate displays rather
than lines forced into one numbered block.

## Cases and custom operators {#sec-math-cases-operators}

Use `\operatorname` when an application needs a named operator that is not
built into ordinary TeX notation. This keeps spacing correct without adding a
backend-specific preamble command. The saturation operator also exercises a
piecewise definition:

$$
\operatorname{sat}_{[\ell,u]}(x) =
\begin{cases}
\ell, & x < \ell, \\
x,    & \ell \le x \le u, \\
u,    & x > u.
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-saturation alt="Piecewise saturation of x between lower and upper bounds"}

The prose can reuse the operator inline as
[$\operatorname{sat}_{[0,1]}(x)$]{.alkahest-math-alt alt="saturate x to the closed interval from zero to one"} without changing its source syntax.

## Matrices and vectors {#sec-math-matrices}

Matrices remain semantic mathematics rather than screenshots. Keep them small
enough for the narrowest edition, or split a derivation before reducing the
type size. A planar rotation is a representative dense display:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}
x' \\ y'
\end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix}
\cos\theta & -\sin\theta \\
\sin\theta &  \cos\theta
\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}
x \\ y
\end{bmatrix}.
$$ {#eq-coordinate-rotation alt="Two-dimensional coordinate rotation matrix"}

Together, @eq-state-update and @eq-coordinate-rotation test references to
structured displays.

## Theorems and proofs {#sec-math-theorems}

Theorem-like blocks use Quarto's reserved semantic identifiers. Their visible
names, counters, and references are generated consistently instead of being
typed into prose.

@thm-saturation-bounds demonstrates a numbered theorem followed immediately by
its unnumbered proof. A proof must remain adjacent to the claim it establishes
and retain a distinct proof label in every output.

::: {#thm-saturation-bounds}
## Saturation bounds

For real numbers [$x$]{.alkahest-math-alt alt="x"},
[$\ell$]{.alkahest-math-alt alt="lower bound ell"}, and
[$u$]{.alkahest-math-alt alt="upper bound u"} with
[$\ell \le u$]{.alkahest-math-alt alt="the lower bound ell is less than or equal to the upper bound u"},
[$\operatorname{sat}_{[\ell,u]}(x)$]{.alkahest-math-alt alt="x saturated to the closed interval from ell to u"} belongs to the closed interval
[$[\ell,u]$]{.alkahest-math-alt alt="the closed interval from ell to u"}.
:::

::: {.proof}
The three branches of @eq-saturation are exhaustive. If
[$x < \ell$]{.alkahest-math-alt alt="x is less than the lower bound ell"}, the result
is [$\ell$]{.alkahest-math-alt alt="the lower bound ell"}; if
[$\ell \le x \le u$]{.alkahest-math-alt alt="x is between ell and u, inclusive"}, the result is
[$x$]{.alkahest-math-alt alt="x"}; and if
[$x > u$]{.alkahest-math-alt alt="x is greater than the upper bound u"}, the result
is [$u$]{.alkahest-math-alt alt="the upper bound u"}. Each result belongs to
[$[\ell,u]$]{.alkahest-math-alt alt="the closed interval from ell to u"}.
:::

## Authoring boundary {#sec-math-boundary}

The supported baseline is portable TeX notation that Pandoc can translate to
native MathML and Typst mathematics. Raw MathJax and raw Typst are reserved for
an explicitly documented output-specific fallback.
Equation numbers and theorem numbers are generated; authors never type them.

Displayed equations and annotated inline-math spans carry meaningful natural-
language alternatives. Surrounding prose must still introduce every symbol
and state the expression's purpose.
